title: Classic Bolognese Ragù

items: ¾ lb mixture of ground beef chuck, pork and veal
Whole nutmeg (about ⅛ tsp freshly grated)
2 cups canned Italian plum tomatoes with juice, torn into pieces
1¼–1½ lb pasta, preferably spaghetti, cooked and drained

steps: Heat the oil, butter and onion in a heavy 3½-quart pot over medium heat. Cook until onion is translucent, then add celery and carrot and cook about 2 minutes, stirring.
Add meats, a large pinch of salt and about 20 turns of finely ground pepper. Break up and cook until no longer pink; do not brown.
Add milk and simmer gently, stirring frequently, until it has evaporated. Stir in about ⅛ tsp freshly grated nutmeg.
Add wine and simmer until evaporated. Stir in tomatoes and juice; when bubbling, reduce heat to the gentlest simmer.
Cook uncovered for at least 3 hours, stirring occasionally. Add ½ cup water as needed to prevent sticking, allowing it to evaporate by the end. Taste and adjust salt.
The source directs adding a remaining tablespoon of butter to the hot pasta. Toss with the ragù and serve with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.
reviewFlags: The ingredients list 3 Tbsp butter, but the directions use butter in the sauce and later call for a remaining tablespoon. Confirm how to divide it.
